indicators.note: ill-treatment of the letters, roughing them up, signals that they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-line verdict on a man loathed for his cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' turns HATEDFORILL into ADOLF HITLER; 'He' is the definition, and the whole clue describes the man too.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points at a particular historical man, the Nazi dictator, whom the clue goes on to describe.

explanation.surface: Someone hoping not to make a poor score.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a DUCK is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to bob down out of its way; in cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a nought, the lowest score.

explanation.surface: A question about buying rounds at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Circuits of a racetrack are rounds; a cat drinks milk by lapping it up with its tongue.

clue.text: One needs a couple of rings to get this number

definitions.text: One needs a couple of rings to get this number

parts.words: One needs a couple of rings to get this number
parts.note: the figure 1 followed by two noughts, the rings, writes this number

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice about how many phone rings it takes to reach a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Written in figures, this count is a digit one followed by two zeros.

explanation.surface: Someone totting up the bar bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To total a column of figures is to tot it up; small measures of spirits are tots.

clue.text: Protected from shock, but still broken-hearted

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the word next to it are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone safe from shocks yet still heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HEARTED; 'broken-hearted' reads as one word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance connected to the ground wire is guarded against electric shock; Americans say grounded.

parts.note: the part of a fraction written below the line, so it sits down in a fraction

explanation.surface: Something only slightly lower than before.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vulgar fraction the lower number, beneath the bar, says into how many parts the whole is divided.

clue.text: Here speaks a writer for a change

indicators.note: doing something for a change means doing it differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An announcement that, unusually, an author will address us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges HERESPEAKSA, with the 'a' as part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard of Avon is the most famous English playwright and poet.

parts.note: keep mum means stay quiet, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A child saying they and their mother cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but means silence, the hush SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth that engage smoothly fit into each other and run together.

parts.note: not sewing but healing treatment carried out with fine needles stuck into the body

explanation.surface: A sewing class for repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese therapy treats ailments by inserting thin needles at points on the skin.

parts.note: a small fastener that catches in a loop, the eye, on clothing

explanation.surface: A flashy new gizmo.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hook-and-eye fastening the curved metal piece catches the loop.

parts.note: one word meaning both a person's temperament, their usual mood, and the way things are set out

explanation.surface: A gloomy piece of music or flower display.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperament is one sense of the word and placement or layout of things is another.

clue.text: Clause in insurance policy motorists will try to avoid

explanation.surface: Small print that drivers dread.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, driving offences add penalty points recorded on the licence.
explanation.definitionFit: An added clause amending an insurance policy has this name; so does a penalty mark recorded on a British driving licence.

indicators.note: to damage something is to knock it out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question whether redoing work can harm it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' rearranges REDOING; 'Cuts' is the past tense of snubbing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately pass them by unacknowledged.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
Ivan is a typical Russian man's name

explanation.surface: A bed shared by plenty of Russians.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch without a back or arms, used for sitting or sleeping.

explanation.surface: Skeleton staying put.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse or skeleton is a person's mortal leftovers; to continue in place is to stay on.

explanation.surface: Percussion at a lively ceilidh.
explanation.definitionFit: Cylinders that cable or film is wound on are drums or spools; Scottish country dances of quick tempo also bear the name.

clue.text: Having eaten a meal I'd end a different shape

indicators.note: giving the letters a different shape means setting them out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone after dinner finding their figure changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking supper or lunch is to have dined, the past participle of dine.

clue.text: Plan to put money in the kitty

indicators.note: the money is placed inside the kitty, as stakes go into the pot

parts.note: a pool of stakes in a card game is the pot
L stands for the pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A scheme to add cash to the communal fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or conspiracy is a plot.

explanation.surface: Plucking feathers from wild birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or spirit makes someone game; wild birds shot for sport are game.

indicators.note: taken out of order, the letters of the city name are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave the Afghan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To baulk something is to hinder or thwart it.

clue.text: A large number put the charge on account

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another follows it, below

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Someone asking that a fee be charged to their account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee but is electrical; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a very big figure.

clue.text: His mark was made in India

definitions.note: a place located in India; the definition names where the region lies

indicators.note: made here means created anew, so the letters are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone who made their name in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges HISMARK; the definition is loose, naming a region partly governed by India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan region in the north of the subcontinent is partly administered by India.

indicators.note: the pronoun is placed inside the word for disgrace

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a disgrace

explanation.surface: A plea to stand by us in our disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold or keep something going is to sustain it.

indicators.note: an upset knocks things over, so the letters come down in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who helps in all sorts of troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: One who saves people from danger is their deliverer.

clue.text: Occasion for the landlord to call

definitions.text: Occasion for the landlord to call

parts.words: Occasion for the landlord to call
parts.note: the pub landlord calls last orders at closing, the moment when drinkers must finish

explanation.surface: A property owner visiting a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs the landlord shouts this word at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Closing hour in a pub is announced by shouting this word.

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A child crying to their mother about an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To injure someone badly, often leaving lasting damage, is to maim.

clue.text: Wooden stick's about right for an annoying child

indicators.note: the stick goes round the letter, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a bat is a wooden stick for hitting a ball; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A cane is the right thing for a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is a brat.

clue.text: Refuse to allow a free vote

indicators.note: set free, the letters are released to settle in another order

explanation.surface: Blocking an unwhipped vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid or block a proposal by authority is to veto it.

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A new type of warning siren.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ALARMSIRENS; 'Novel' poses as an adjective. SILAS MARNER is George Eliot's novel about a miserly weaver.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's 1861 book about a weaver is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Is the possessor of topless dresses

indicators.note: the word loses its top, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone owning revealing dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something as one's property is to possess it.

indicators.note: out means unsettled or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber knocked unconscious, as in a boxing count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MOUNTAINEER; 'out for the count' suggests a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally or listing of items one by one is an enumeration.
